title: Chestnut Hill Realty plans to install AI-powered license plate reader cameras in South Brookline - Brookline.News
summary: Chestnut Hill Realty, a private real estate company, plans to install Flock Safety license plate reader cameras near its Hancock Village property in South Brookline, MA, and will share the data with Brookline and Boston police via an MOU. The Police Commissioner's Advisory Committee voted 5-0 to sign the MOU, though ACLU of Massachusetts and one committee member raised privacy and civil rights concerns.

key_quotes.quote: Unregulated, this technology facilitates the mass tracking of every single person's movements on the road
Chestnut Hill Realty, as the customer, owns the data collected by the readers and can share it with whomever the company wishes, according to Flock.
Brookline police will have access to a dashboard that will save license plate information from cars which have passed by the cameras for 30 days.
I am very concerned that someone driving by Chestnut Hill Realty properties … could get tagged, not see the sign and that we could be facilitating abuses
